answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via hardware remote attestation. Agents execute inside secure enclaves that anchor identities to physical silicon. Each network inlet verifies this attestation echo, forcing an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of procuring dedicated cryptographic processors per persona. This restriction stems the tide of synthetic bot swarms. However, enclaves remain vulnerable to silicon side-channel leaks and centralized manufacturer trust.
